Descartes Systems Group has launched Descartes Spot , a new tool that helps freight forwarders quickly get spot-rate quotes for customers. The company says forwarders can answer 90% of customer quote requests in 30 seconds or less.
What’s Related
The cloud -based tool is part of Descartes' broker and forwarder enterprise systems suite. It pulls live carrier rates, schedules, fees, surcharges, and transit times into one place, so sales teams don't have to build each quote by hand. Users enter a port pairing and immediately get several shipping options, each with routes, schedules, transit times and fully calculated costs.
That's different from how many forwarders quote today. Pricing a spot shipment often means digging through carrier websites, plugging numbers into spreadsheets, and waiting hours or even days to send an answer back.
RELATED: Women in Supply Chain: Cyndi Brandt of Descartes Systems Group
Why speed matters
“Speed and transparency are real competitive differentiators in freight forwarding,” said Henning Voss, VP of Product Management at Descartes. “Forwarding is a fast-moving, high-pressure business . Sales teams are under significant strain, and facing huge volumes of requests from customers that require manual, time-consuming work. In a competitive market, the first credible offer often wins.”
Voss said the goal is to let forwarders reply while a deal is still on the table. “This means forwarders can respond while the opportunity is still live and put their energy where it counts: their market knowledge, their relationships, and the deal itself.”
How Spot helps freight forwarders
Along with faster quotes, Descartes Spot lets teams:
Give customers multiple routing and departure options across trade lanes
Save, manage, send, and track quotes in one place
Let business development staff build quotes on their own, without waiting on operations
Set pricing controls to protect margins
Check prices against the market using benchmarking from Xeneta
That last point matters for forwarders worried that faster quoting means underpricing. Xeneta's rate data lets a sales rep compare a quote to the market before sending it.
Forwarders as sales shops
Ken Wood, EVP of Product Management at Descartes, said the launch reflects how the forwarding business is changing.
“Leading freight forwarders are increasingly operating as growth-focused sales organizations, where responsiveness and customer experience play a larger role in winning business,” Wood said. “By removing the delays associated with manual spot quoting, Descartes Spot helps forwarders respond to more opportunities, improve win rates and drive profitable growth.”
